description: Latency x host-response timescale (n = 4, n_R = n), set B' signal and host response. The response_timescale tau_R divides alpha_m, delta_m, alpha_p, delta_p, so the priming curve stretches (t_1/2 = 0.41 tau_R, t* = 1.81 tau_R) at fixed ceiling phi_inf = 0.952. Fronts outrun their warning when t* exceeds the lead time T(c) = Lambda_eff / (lambda_s c) - tau (1 - n_R / n) (eq. 43); long latency slows the front, which can either let the bin convert infected cells (§ 3.7) or silence the signal (c < c_sil = 0.224, § 3.3). Theory-based layout, not yet confirmed by runs of the revised model. RNA-protein host response of the first review's revision of Oct 24 2026 (eq. 22); uses the density cutoff (no infection below V_ext = p_ext, removal at rate 5).

expected.long latency: stall by conversion during latency (§ 3.7) or a steady silent front (c ~ c_sil); this map tests which
expected.earlier runs: with the Erlang priming chain (SISV8/9), long latency silenced the signal and gave steady fronts
